ptr.theme: Blood Debt set lands well; hero race too close to call
ptr.summary: A Death's Advance theorycrafter's read of the redesigned Venomous Abyss set is that Blizzard fixed the consistency problem: where the scrapped Crimson Scourge design paid out unevenly by target count and hero tree, the Blood Debt set is worth a steady +6-8% damage for both hero talents at every target count checked, with only a small gap between them. What it is not is a defensive set — survivability impact is measured as mostly negligible — and the San'layn-versus-Deathbringer question is left explicitly open: his gut says Deathbringer holds M+, but San'layn gained enough this patch that he won't take a strong stance before live data.
changes: The implemented Blood Debt set matches the 06-30 preview with seemingly no modification. Mechanics as tested: stacks have no duration and persist through combat drops, Death Strike cleave grants only one stack, stacking continues during the 10%-Strength buff, and the 10-stack itself is the enhanced-Marrowrend trigger — no second buff to track.

Measured M+ gains (from his 2026-07-21 Death's Advance post, not the guide): Deathbringer +6% single-target / +7% at 5-10 targets; San'layn +7% / +8% — far more even than the scrapped Crimson Scourge design (+6/+4.5 and +10/+8), and consistent across target counts.
At 10 stacks the enhanced Marrowrend becomes a high-priority cast; the damage is strong enough that sitting on a 10-stack indefinitely is not worthwhile.

Season 2 re-buffs The Blood is Life (figures from the 2026-07-21 Death's Advance post, not the guide): base Blood Beast and explosion damage +1400%, Pact of the San'layn +50% — the one Blood mechanic that scales exponentially with target count, and historically the piece modeling underweights.

San'layn also picks up Blood-Soaked Ground physical mitigation 5% → 8% (07-21) and disproportionately benefits from the Dance of Midnight bug fix, since its higher haste procs Dancing Rune Weapon more often.

Historical note: Wowhead's Mandl reviewed the original Crimson Scourge / Death-and-Decay set as "a complete miss" — that Negative applied to a design previewed away on 06-30 and replaced in the 07-08 build; this writeup reviews its replacement.
ptr.set2: Blood Debt on Death Strike (to 5% Strength, then a 10%-Strength enhanced Marrowrend at 10 stacks) — measured at a consistent damage gain for both hero trees, with the stack bookkeeping deliberately forgiving: no duration, no combat-drop loss, no cleave multi-stacking.
ptr.set4: The enhanced Marrowrend's +3 Bone Shield and Shadow AoE make it a high-priority cast at 10 stacks. Across both bonuses the set reads as offense-only — survivability impact mostly negligible — so the old complaint that a tank's set carries no defensive value still applies to the numbers, if not to the design's coherence.
ptr.watch: The hero-talent call is still the thing to watch, and in his shipped 12.1 M+ guide the author has stopped calling it: the Upfront Recommendation now reads "Either", with "no firm recommendation being made for hero talents" — a move off the loosely-held Deathbringer stance of his 07-21 read. His reasoning is that changing tier-set dynamics plus damage and minor defensive tuning are on net to San'layn's benefit, making the M+ choice ambiguous once more after Deathbringer was "fairly dominant" through Midnight S1; what stays unsettled is whether San'layn can muster a damage advantage large enough to outweigh Deathbringer's better mitigation, EHP and snap threat on pull. He also lays out why prediction keeps failing for this spec: Essence of the Blood Queen models assume melee uptime reality never delivers; The Blood is Life's exponential AoE scaling isn't weighted by standard target-count methodology; the defensive value of extra Death Strikes is ambiguous; and Deathbringer's smoother pull setup and threat are invisible to all three metrics.

ptr.theme: Burst redistributed into sustain, and the raid-testing read is good
ptr.summary: Icy Veins' Season 2 raid write-up reads Frost DK as having a lot of power shifted out of its cooldowns and into a more sustained damage profile, without changing how the spec plays: most of the changes just move damage numbers around, so the Season 1 rotation carries over. They note it is no longer the hyper-bursty spec it was, but since every other burst cooldown was nerfed too it still sports some of the highest burst in the game while now also carrying solid sustained DPS. Their stated evidence for the ranking is that Frost's performance has been great during raid testing, with Death Grip called out as highly useful utility on the many add fights.
changes: Power shifted out of cooldowns and towards baseline/sustained damage — the core rotation is unchanged from Season 1 because most of the changes only move damage numbers around.
Still one of the highest-burst specs in relative terms: Icy Veins' point is that competing burst cooldowns were nerfed as well, so Frost keeps its burst identity while gaining sustain.
Cited as performing well in 12.1 raid testing, with Death Grip valued as raid utility on add-heavy fights.
ptr.watch: The read is a tier-list author's, written before live play — Icy Veins place Frost DK at A+ for Season 2 raid, so the claim to test at launch is whether the added sustain really compensates for the reduced cooldown burst.

ptr.theme: Minion pruning + an all-passive tier set
ptr.summary: 12.1 cuts Unholy's active minion count (Army of the Dead rework, Reanimation becomes Lord of the Dead) and reshuffles burst damage, but Taeznak finds the execution half-baked: commanding your ghouls reduces to mindlessly spamming Scourge Strike, and the tier set is entirely passive. He likes the concepts — "I can see the intention, and it's incredible" — but says nearly every piece needs "a LOT of work."
changes: Army of the Dead no longer summons extra ghouls — you command 8 fixed ghouls via Death Order / Epidemic Order, picked by enemy count rather than the player; the net rotation is mindless Scourge Strike spam with Sudden Doom procs devalued.

Knock-on breakage: Doomed Bidding doesn't work at all (likely a bug), and Outnumber may fall from always-taken capstone to skipped outright, dragging lesser-ghoul talents (Infected Claws, Commander of the Dead, etc.) down with it.

Soul Reaper now consumes up to 3 Lesser Ghoul stacks instead of 2 Putrefy charges — forcing extra 2-rune Festering Strikes and courting resource starvation in execute, without fixing the old Commander-of-the-Dead overlap problem.

Army ghouls last 30s and the new Lord of the Dead lich concentrates damage back into burst windows — contradicting the stated burst-reduction goal; the messaging is 'confusing and contradictory' while sustained damage goes untouched.

PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): overperformance nerf after first Heroic raid testing — all damage −8%, Lord of the Dead −25%, Magus of the Dead −15%, Lesser Ghoul damage −15%, Putrefy/Pestilence/Infected Claw/Virulent Plague −25%, Necrotic Coil −18%; Rider of the Apocalypse's Whitemane Death Coil/Undeath −25%.

Forum post #12 (2026-07-08, follow-up bug fix): Blizzard says the build-68569 tuning pass itself had a bug — the blanket all-damage reduction is corrected from −8% to −3%. Also fixed Nazgrim's Conquest incorrectly granting Strength when Magus of the Dead is sacrificed for Lord of the Dead (and from critters/low-level targets).
ptr.set2: Magi and Liches swap to a stronger Necrotic Bolt and Withering Grasp — "vaguely interesting" for spotlighting the new lich, but entirely passive with zero player control.
ptr.set4: +130% to both spells against enemies below 35% health — a flat execute amp Taeznak calls "about as bland and boring as it could possibly get"; the piece that "needs a LOT of work," and rare in being less interesting than the 2pc.
ptr.watch: Unholy enters 12.1 from an S1-topping baseline (M+ S-tier across boards), so a trim was expected — the complaint is direction, not numbers. Watch whether Blizzard picks a lane (sustained spec vs ~80%-of-damage-in-cooldowns), fixes the non-functional Doomed Bidding, and adds any decision-making to the one-button Army rotation before ship.

ptr.theme: Essence Break bought back into the rotation
ptr.summary: The 7/21 pass is a net buff the author reads as decisive for Essence Break: a flat 5% to all damage, a 35% buff to Essence Break's initial hit, and a 4-set that adds another 35% on top — enough, in his words, that the talent will now simply be played. changes: All damage +5%; Essence Break initial damage +35%.
The Venomous Abyss 4-set now raises Essence Break's initial damage by 35% (was 25%), stacking with the baseline buff.
Immolation Aura damage -8%, with Burning Hatred's Fury per tick cut to 30 (was 40) — the spec is deliberately made less reliant on Immolation Aura for both damage and Fury.
Demon Blades Fury generation raised to 10-16 (was 8-15), partly backfilling the Burning Hatred loss.
ptr.set4: The 4-set's Essence Break bonus rose 25% → 35% in the same build, compounding the baseline Essence Break buff rather than substituting for it.
ptr.watch: The author had not yet simmed the changes when he posted — the read is on the tuning numbers, not on output. How much of the Immolation Aura Fury loss the Demon Blades increase actually replaces is the open question.

ptr.theme: Void Meta flattened → Soulburst Reap set
ptr.summary: Blizzard flattens Devourer's all-in Void Meta profile — Mastery's in-Meta bonus cut 66%, offset by a rare 20% all-ability aura buff — and the author judges the stated goal achieved: slightly less damage inside the cooldown, significantly more outside it. The Soulburst tier set is "AWESOME" and rotationally transformative, turning Reap into a main focus; the author is having a LOT of fun on PTR.
changes: Mastery: Monster Within's Void Meta bonus cut 66% — the author's own 45% in-Meta mastery drops to 15% on identical gear — pushing gearing toward Crit/Haste come 12.1.
All ability damage +20% — a 'GIGANTIC' aura buff, rare at this size; with nothing else changing it still nets roughly a 10% loss for Annihilator, before retuning.
Impending Apocalypse star ramp 30% → 20% (a 5-star window's final star falls from +120% to +80%); Void Meta's Void Ray bonus 67% → 40%; Consume +60%.

The rebalance hits Annihilator harder than Void-Scarred — likely forcing a hero-talent swap — while Void-Scarred's no-synergy caster/melee split (and Devourer's Bite, which 'needs to go') is left unaddressed.
Demon Hunters can now equip daggers — fun access to the new cantrip daggers, otherwise uneventful.
PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): all ability damage increased by 10% (an underperformance buff), while sibling spec Havoc took −5%.

Follow-up tuning (7/21, revised for the 7/23 mini-patch) nets to almost nothing in a Fel Hammer theorycrafter's read: Collapsing Star +12% against Otherworldly Focus 35% → 30% leaves a small Void-Scarred Caster buff and only a slight Annihilator buff — far less than Annihilator needs to compete with Void-Scarred — while Eradicate -6% is a 6% cut to the whole Reap/Cull/Eradicate suite.
ptr.set2: Soulburst: a 4+ soul Reap has a 20% chance (deck-of-cards system, so low variance) to make the next Consume instant and explode in AoE — only 1-2% overall, plus minor instant-cast QoL.
ptr.set4: Where the set shines: Soulburst generates 8 Soul Fragments plus Moment of Craving and Reap gains 20% damage — one of the kit's most efficient soul generators, "rotationally transformative," and a bigger win for Void-Scarred than Annihilator. (Historical pre-August-18 values: the live set now generates 2 Soul Fragments and increases Reap damage by 10%; the quoted evaluation concerns the earlier design.)
ptr.watch: Eradicate currently can't proc Soulburst — a significant AoE/cleave proc loss the author calls a bug that "needs to be fixed ASAP" — and Void-Scarred's caster/melee dysfunction went untouched. From today's S/A-tier baseline the author still expects a "great spot" at 12.1 launch, provided that fix lands. As of the 7/23 revision the Annihilator/Void-Scarred gap had not closed: the same tuning that slightly helped Annihilator helped Void-Scarred Caster more.

changes: The 4-set is on the weaker side numerically and probably needs a buff; the rest of the pass is a handful of changes that don't really change your gameplay.

With Wingleader's scaling gone, Scalecommander sits 7.7% behind Chronowarden in all content — "just dead", after being 10-15% ahead in Mythic+ — and Augmentation's AoE has no replacement for it. The author's expectation is that the spec is no longer M+ dominant or invited to groups, while raid is likely okay but not exceptional.
changes: Scalecommander is 7.7% behind Chronowarden in all content, having previously been ~10-15% ahead in Mythic+ while Chronowarden was considered unplayable there.
Augmentation's AoE cannot leverage the old Wingleader scaling, taking the spec out of M+ dominance and, in the author's read, out of invites.
The new set is built around Fate Mirror, so with weaker personal damage and fewer duplicates the spec leans much harder on ally performance.
Chronowarden's Double-time change is a net ~1% loss; Eons-first openers are roughly equal.
Every hero-talent and class build is the same across all content — Rumbling Earth, Mighty Inferno, Threads, Plot the Future — because nothing else is tuned to compete.
ptr.set4: The new Chronowarden 4-set is quite good — about 0.5% ahead of 2+2, and clearly ahead once the ilvl difference is counted. On Scalecommander the author still runs 2pc+2pc.
ptr.watch: Raid is the surviving case: possibly picked up in a race for Evoker buffs like Time Spiral, though Preservation is preferred as it stands. Earlier (7/8) another Wyrmrest voice called Wingleader "found dead in the gutter" and judged the Command Squadron and Melt Armor buffs nowhere near compensating — with the caveat that there was still time before release for another iteration. The community's formal Scalecommander case is filed at us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/t/scalecommander-changes/2325059 (Xephyris, 07-08).

ptr.summary: Peak of Serenity's Brewmaster writer reads the 12.1 pass as deliberately flat: nearly every class change is a net-neutral offset for players and creatures gaining 25% health and damage at max level, not a power shift. The set bonuses are judged fairly bland for now — extra Fire damage feeding Vital Flame is welcome, and the 4-piece amounts to a stronger Mystic Touch. The one genuine unknown is a datamined doubling of Celestial Brew and Celestial Infusion's cooldown AND absorb, which never made official notes.
changes: The absorb/heal-percentage buffs (Celestial Brew/Infusion +25%, Staggering Strikes +25%, Awakening Spirit +25%, Vital Flame 40% → 50%, Chi Transfer 50% → 60%, Vigorous Expulsion, Spirit of the Ox) are scaling offsets for the 25% health/creature-damage increase, not net gains.
The max-health increase slightly reduces Gift of the Ox sphere spawn frequency by the mechanic's design — noted as unlikely to be felt in practice, based on past instances.

Datamined in the 06-30 build, undocumented: Celestial Brew and Celestial Infusion recharge doubled to 1.5 minutes with absorbs doubled to match. Possibly a bug, but the paired change reads intentional — one guess is making Light Brewing's percentage CDR feel weightier against Training of Niuzao.

07-21: Flurry Strikes' Physical damage now correctly benefits from Bring Me Another and the Venomous Abyss 4-set (bug fix). 12.1 sims remain work-in-progress through the tuning churn, so no meaningful sim delta lands from it.
ptr.set2: The ignited Keg Smash is more Fire damage in the kit, which Vital Flame converts to healing — the author's one warm note on an otherwise bland pair.
ptr.set4: Read as "stronger Mystic Touch": an 8% Physical-damage amplifier plus a fire patch. The Scorched / Hot Potato cooldown-manager entries presumably track these ignited-keg effects.
ptr.watch: The Celestial Brew/Infusion doubling is the thing to resolve — bug or redesign. The author's own counsel is to test it on PTR and leave feedback before concluding it's terrible; a 1.5-minute defensive cadence would change brew rhythm more than anything else in the pass.

ptr.summary: A ~30% cut to the damage-to-healing conversion on Spinning Crane Kick / Way of the Crane, offset by a Jadefire buff. The author is positive overall, though hero-tree balance goes untouched.
changes: Damage→heal conversion cut ~30% (SCK / Way of the Crane).
Spinning Crane Kick's effective target threshold shifts ~3 → 8.
Jadefire buffed to compensate for the conversion loss.
PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): Spinning Crane Kick damage +10%, plus a fix so Temple Training's SCK increase now applies to Mistweaver.

A Peak of Serenity changelog tracks the rebalance landing harder than the notes read one build at a time: Way of the Crane's transfer fell 340% → 280% at reveal, and after the later Spinning Crane Kick nerf-then-partial-revert the author measures the total package at -15.3% week-over-week and -29.9% versus live.

Two blanket healing cuts landed along the way (-3% at reveal, -7% in a later hotfix wave), traded against Mastery: Gust of Mists +50% twice (baseline mastery 249.48% after the second), mana returns +20% across most sources (Mana Tea 5,400 → 6,480 per stack), and Rising Mist's internal cooldown halved to 500ms — the Mastery-forward shift the developers said they wanted, enforced by nerfing the alternatives.
Morning Breeze was cut 60% explicitly to keep pace with the Gust of Mists increases — the developers' note frames it as holding the talent's effectiveness level, not nerfing it.
ptr.set2: Supports the Jadefire-forward direction.
ptr.set4: Leans into the retuned kit.
ptr.watch: Hero-tree balance (Conduit of the Celestials clearly over Master of Harmony) is left unaddressed. Baseline is already dominant — raid-S / M+-S. The Peak of Serenity read to carry forward: the damage-to-healing conversion loop is roughly 30% weaker than live even after the partial Spinning Crane Kick walk-back, so how much of the Positive design read survives contact with the final tuning is the open question.

ptr.theme: From "zero changes" to a better spec by three corrections
ptr.summary: Clarius's running read spans the whole PTR cycle: a reveal with literally zero Holy changes beyond the set, a 4-piece upgraded from coin-flip to guaranteed Infusion on Holy Light, an accidental no-Holy-Shock build born from that same 4-piece, a 50% Holy Shock healing buff that briefly made every build equal, and finally a tier-set-attached Holy Light mana increase that kills the degenerate build for good. His close: throughput is up significantly, Eternal Flame is now the default spender with a better healing profile, and he is personally pleased with where it landed.
changes: 4pc buffed on 6/30 from a 50% chance to a 100% chance for Holy Light to grant Infusion of Light — 'a great change,' you can now always rely on Holy Light for Infusions and stop spamming them back to back.

6/30 also brought Eternal Flame closer to Light of Dawn, opening builds that drop Unending Light / Breaking Dawn and enable Empyrean Legacy / Truth Prevails with EF as the main HP spender — better healing profile and more fun.
Pillars of Light + the EF buff + the new set make Beacon of Virtue far more appealing; for M+, where EF was already best, it's a straight buff.
2pc increases Infusion of Light additively: Infused Flash of Light heals +275% instead of +200% (a 25% bump) and Greater Judgment hits +225% instead of +150% (a 30% bump).

PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): broad buff for talent diversity — all healing +8%, Holy Shock +10%, the 2-set now doubles Infusion of Light (100%, was 75%), plus buffs to Truth Prevails, Saved by the Light, Overflowing Light, Awakening, Ringing of the Heavens and more.

PTR 2026-07-23 (post-writeup tuning): Blizzard found the 4-set was leaving Holy Paladin more mana-efficient than intended and added a 60% Holy Light mana-cost increase to the 4-set, while raising overall healing by 5% to compensate — a net efficiency check, not a redesign of the Infusion mechanic.

The 4-piece's guaranteed Infusion enabled a "no Holy Shock" build — skipping Holy Shock entirely funds Holy Light on every non-proc GCD, spends less mana than normal play, and eliminates weak filler casts. He published proof-of-concept (log + video) while predicting it would be fixed before launch.

The subsequent 50% Holy Shock healing buff (plus 11% mana cut) was far larger than he expected: post-buff raid testing had normal and no-HS builds, Herald and Lightsmith alike, performing so evenly that "you could play whichever you prefer".

The fix arrived as a tier-set-attached ~50% Holy Light mana increase — killing no-HS for good while leaving the satisfying always-proc 4-piece intact, with a 5% healing compensation. His read: strange to tie a malus to a set, but the right call versus nerfing the 4-piece, and precedent says spell nerfs made for sets don't get reverted later.

End state: Season-1-like play but with everything healing significantly more, Eternal Flame ahead of Light of Dawn as the default spender, Judgment over unbuffed Flash of Light thanks to the 2-piece, and mana effectively under your control through Holy Light volume.
ptr.set2: A pretty standard set — makes Infusions feel better and more important not to waste (+25% on Infused Flash of Light, +30% on Greater Judgment), but not particularly strong compared to other healers' 2pc bonuses. (Pre-07-08 — Infusion of Light effectiveness was since raised to 100%.)
ptr.set4: Originally a 50% chance for Holy Light to grant Infusion of Light — which also caused wasted procs since you don't know you've proc'd until you've already queued the next spell. The 6/30 buff to a guaranteed 100% chance fixes that and is 'a great change': Holy Light is now a reliable Infusion generator, no more back-to-back spamming, and much more fun to play. (07-23 PTR: a 60% Holy Light mana-cost increase was added to the 4-set to rein in its mana efficiency, paired with a 5% overall healing buff — the reliability the writeup praises is unchanged.)
ptr.watch: His remaining complaints are structural, not tuning: too many kiss/curse talents (Call of the Righteous, Seraphic Barrier) whose downsides outweigh their point, and Inflorescence of the Sunwell — near-mandatory with this set — gated behind three mediocre talents. Lightsmith remains a no-Holy-Shock-style spender at heart and tested strongest with Beacon of Virtue by a small margin, but the busier rotation makes normal Herald the likely best build for most players.

ptr.theme: Talent reshuffle and a damage-amp set, offset by quiet nerfs
ptr.summary: The Hammer of Wrath crew (Woliance, Fluttershy) read 12.1 as a mixed bag: a talent-tree reshuffle opens up new pairings (Sentinel now sits alongside Avenging Wrath) and a Crusader Strike tier set leans hard into damage, but a string of undocumented nerfs to Divine Exaction, Blessed Assurance and Glory of the Vanguard quietly claw offense back, with a bug list still pending fixes.
changes: Talent shuffle: Blessed Word (WoG crit) becomes a choice node with Valiant Crusade; Sentinel is now pickable together with Avenging Wrath (moved to the old Empyrean Authority spot), and Empyrean Authority slides into the old Sanctified Wrath slot.
Undocumented nerf: Divine Exaction cut to +50% extra damage, down from +150%.
Undocumented nerf: Blessed Assurance now +100% extra on Blessed Hammer / Hammer of the Righteous after a spender, down from +200%.
Undocumented nerf: Glory of the Vanguard secondary damage reduced to 50%, down from 100%.
Undocumented buff: Undying Embers now heals for at least 125% of Refining Fire damage, scaling up to 300% as HP drops.

PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): Lightsmith's Divine Guidance redesigned (each Holy Power ability empowers the next Consecration to deal split Holy damage and heal up to 3 allies); several fixes/QoL (Blessed Word, Valiant Crusade no longer cancels on death, Improved Ardent Defender fatal-damage indicator) and Guardian of Ancient Kings' initial cooldown raised to 8s.
ptr.set2: The "Crusader Strike" set (Blessed Hammer, Hammer of the Righteous, Crusader Strike and Judgment) is a pure damage amp — those hits deal 20% increased damage, or 60% if the hit crits. The crew reads it as a straightforward offensive lever that rewards building around crit to hit the higher tier, doubling down on Prot's damage rotation rather than adding defensive value. (Pre-07-14 — the crit bonus was since halved: 100% additional damage, was 200%.)
ptr.watch: Note: the sources describe the tier set as a single combined mechanic and do not cleanly split a 2pc vs 4pc bonus, so the whole tier-set read sits in set2 and set4 is left empty. These are PTR values on top of an early, still-shifting tree — several of the nerfs are undocumented (Fluttershy) and the Hammer of Wrath Discord is tracking a live bug list, so the 60%-on-crit set payoff and the net offensive floor could both move before 12.1 ships. Treat the numbers as against the 12.0.7 baseline.

ptr.theme: Smoother Holy Power, but a controversial 4-set that fights the spec's identity
ptr.summary: Bolas's Wowhead review. The 12.1 changes make Holy Power generation far more predictable and much faster — decoupling Ret from needing a Shaman's Skyfury and letting Art of War stack twice, both of which Bolas thinks feel genuinely better. But he argues the direction keeps pushing Ret toward "spend Holy Power ASAP with little agency," Avenging Wrath eats a notable burst nerf, and the real story is the tier set: a solid, inoffensive 2pc paired with a 4pc that's "one of the most controversial set bonuses in the Retribution community in recent memory" for forcing you to use the "wrong" spender for the target count.
changes: Crusading Strikes flips from −20% to +15% auto-attack speed and no longer procs off Skyfury or generates Holy Power from extra Skyfury attacks — roughly 20% more hits, decoupling Ret from needing a Shaman in group and smoothing (but flooding) Holy Power generation.

Art of War can now accumulate one extra charge (Apex Talent: Light Within Rank 1) — Bolas's favourite change; removes the awkward Holy Power loss from having to instantly spend procs. Side effect: makes Improved Blade of Justice much worse, since its use case was banking charges for procs.

Damage shuffled out of cooldowns into the core kit: Blade of Justice +40%; Templar Strike/Slash, Judgment, Hammer of Wrath all +50%; Final Verdict and Divine Storm +15%. Offsetting nerfs: Art of War's Blade of Justice bonus 150%→80%, Divine Toll's Judgment 100%→50%, Light Within Rank 3 damage −25%.

Avenging Wrath now grants +15% damage and crit (was +20%) — Bolas calls it a fairly severe nerf given Ret's AW window wasn't especially strong to begin with, though 12.1 is bringing cooldown nerfs to most specs.
Healing buffed across the board: Flash of Light, Word of Glory, and Eternal Flame all +25%. Templar's Hammer of Light now costs 3 Holy Power (was 5) but deals −30% damage (does not affect PvP).

PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): all damage −6%, and the Venomous Abyss 4-set reworked — consuming Divine Purpose now grants Divine Arbiter (empowering other Holy Power spenders to hit for Holy AoE; Divine Arbiter damage +35%), an attempt to address the tier set's pain points while keeping its identity.
ptr.set2: Divine Purpose gains an additional 10% chance to activate, and consuming it grants Divine Power — +10% Holy damage done for 12 seconds. Bolas calls it "pretty solid and inoffensive": a clean, uncontroversial throughput bonus.
ptr.set4: Consuming Divine Purpose with Divine Storm grants 2 stacks of Divine Arbiter, making your next Final Verdicts unleash an AoE Holy nuke (8-yd splash) — but only if no Arbiter stacks are already active, so once you hold stacks you must spend Divine Purpose on Final Verdict (the single-target spender) instead. "One of the most controversial set bonuses in the Retribution community in recent memory": it forces the "wrong" spender for the target count, which the official feedback thread explicitly flagged as a degenerate/unintended rotation impact. Bolas thinks it misses the mark — easy to accidentally misplay and punishing when you do, yet with a low skill ceiling once learned, bucking Ret's beginner-friendly Dragonflight-era identity. ptr.theme: Great spec changes, a placeholder tier set
ptr.summary: The fuller Wowhead review. Whispyr calls the spec changes genuinely great and well-executed — the reworked Implacable apex now refunds Energy on Envenom cast (no more intentionally letting the buff drop), a new Unstable Toxin capstone, talent repositioning, and Iron Wire now spreading make the rotation feel noticeably smoother with real build choices. But the patch is 'lacking otherwise': the tier set is another bland '10% Mastery' stat-stick that misses Blizzard's own complexity/impact goals, and the bigger pain points — Deathstalker's clunk and the dead bottom third of the class tree — went untouched.
changes: Implacable apex reworked (the headline change): Envenom +10% damage and now refunds 2 Energy per combo point on cast — no more waiting for the buff to drop. A welcome simplification; the S1 buff was notoriously buggy to track.
New capstone Unstable Toxin: Envenom +18% damage but -2s buff duration — a kiss-curse rewarding tight Envenom-window management, most practical in heavy AoE.

Iron Wire now spreads (via Crimson Tempest) and its stealth / Improved-Garrote Garrotes silence for 5s — new M+ utility vs a ~1-2% DPS choice. Internal Bleeding no longer spreads (self-cast Rupture/Kidney Shot; cover it with Canny Strikes).
Energy economy retuned: Dashing Scoundrel now grants baseline regen, Motivated Murderer 30% (was 20%), Blindside proc down — leaving Assa slightly faster, ~10-15% more Energy scaling into 5-8T AoE.

Bleed buffs (Shrouded Suffocation 30%, Avulsion 25%, Rapid Injection 20/40%) plus repositioning give a ~10% uplift in 2-4T cleave; Deathmark (75%, was 100%) and Kingsbane (-15%) nerfed to match the patch; +3% all damage baseline.
Class / hero: Thistle Tea is now a choice node (auto-at-low-Energy vs active-only), Atrophic Poison buffed to 4% / 60s; Fatebound's Deal Fate extra combo point cut to 60% (was 100%).

PTR build (2026-07-21): all damage dealt +6% and Apex Talent Implacable Strike +15%; the Venomous Abyss 4-set Amplifying Poison bonus raised to 3% per stack (was 2%) — a straight numbers pass that leaves the set's design (the one Whispyr flagged as a flat 'Mastery %' stat-stick) unchanged.
ptr.set2: A generic Nature-damage buff with no gameplay change and no build impact — Whispyr reads the whole set as another 'Mastery %' stat-stick in disguise.
ptr.set4: The bleed half of the same 'Mastery %' formula. Whispyr's big disappointment: blander than even the Season 1 set, it creates no gameplay and no build decisions and misses Blizzard's stated 'more complex / more impactful' goals — reads as a placeholder or in need of a full rework. Amplifying Poison stays the standard poison pick.
ptr.watch: Tuning isn't there yet: Unstable Toxin's -2s downside is currently 'actively crippling' in single target — it can cost more Envenom damage than the +18% adds and fights Rapid Injection's 40%, leaving you at the mercy of crit RNG; Iron Wire's new spread doesn't refresh on reapplication (possibly a bug). The louder critique is what went unaddressed: Deathstalker stays buggy, unintuitive and rarely played, and the bottom third of the class tree (Soothing Darkness / Subterfuge / Without a Trace, Thistle Tea, Cold Blooded Killer, Supercharger) stays bland — the obvious place to add the 'build options' Blizzard said they wanted.

The 07-15 Killing Spree pass is judged genuinely good — KS no longer fights Supercharge and flows under Adrenaline Rush, worth about 3% — with two corrections to Blizzard's own wording: Ruthlessness means KS at 7 combo points still slightly overcaps, and Adrenaline Rush's execution speedup is 25%, not the stated 20%.

Standing caveats from the sim side: 2-3-target cleave energy strain persists into Season 2, and the spec's famously wide RNG range isn't narrowing — Fast Action may widen it.

Ravenholdt's reveal-day read (06-18) was brutal: the Shadowcraft change alone cuts combo point and energy generation an estimated 20-30%, the 4-piece desyncs Shadow Dance from Secret Technique, and the on-PTR spec was described as having "no cleave, no burst, no priority damage and no notable utility" — "to say I am disappointed would be a massive understatement."

Then the tuning turned again: an 8% blanket nerf on 07-08 (with the caveat that other strong specs were nerfed too), and by 07-21 the Goremaw buff only promotes it "from underwhelming to mediocre" while the spec "remains completely over."

07-23 datamine: the SEASON 1 set is nerfed from ~7-8% to ~4-5% — expected, aimed at retiring 2p2p into Season 2, though possibly not enough to beat the ilvl upgrade on set slots, so 2p2p may survive early season.
ptr.set2: Placeholder-tier value.
ptr.set4: Essentially just pushes more Backstab — no new decision or identity.
ptr.watch: Comes into 12.1 at raid-A / M+-A, so it's nerfing from a fine spot — but the set is the least inspired of the tracked Rogues. The Ravenholdt arc to carry: reveal-day despair, a 06-30 walk-back that restored resources and goodwill, then renewed nerfs through late July — the burst identity loss the original Negative describes was never restored, only the resource floor.

ptr.theme: Fun to play and buffed, but old structural baggage lingers
ptr.summary: Wordup's Wowhead review. The 12.1 changes are almost universally buffs (Totemic ~+3%, Stormbringer +3–5% by target count) and he strongly agrees the reworked spec's gameplay is 'very good'; the Season 2 tier set is a big step up from S1's whelming offering and looks like a solid all-rounder. But the article's weight is on 'baggage' that has lingered since Beta: an all-or-nothing cooldown profile on both hero trees, the frustrating Doom Winds/Ascendance 'deck of cards' RNG, lost priority/funnel damage, and Totemic slipping behind Stormbringer again — the same War Within reset pattern.
changes: Core buffs aimed at the weak downtime between cooldowns: Lightning Bolt & Chain Lightning +20%; Lava Lash & Stormstrike +15%; melee +15%.
Doom Winds now increases Windfury Weapon activation chance by 50% (was 100%) — trims the mass-AoE Windfury spike, felt mainly by Totemic.
Stormbringer nerf: Tempest main-target −10%, secondary-target −30%.
Totemic nerf: Surging Totem Tremor −15%, Surging Bolt −10%.

Net is still almost universally a buff (Totemic ~+3%, −1% in mass AoE; Stormbringer +3–5% by target count), but Wordup notes the devs' stated goal of shifting damage OUT of cooldown windows wasn't really achieved — only Totemic's Surging Totem took a real hit and it was mostly offset.

PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): Venomous Abyss 4-set fixes — Short Circuit now actually gets consumed, Crash Lightning (Unleashed) again hits all targets, and the 4-set now boosts the Crash Lightning weapon-enhancement damage (averaged across active stacks).
ptr.set2: Reworked this week and much improved over S1. Built around Voltaic Blaze; the previous version had a single-target 'killswitch' (lost its 200% multiplier the moment a 2nd target appeared) — now a strong, self-sufficient universal bonus (its own Fire Nova procs) with the set's value weighted heavily here. Wordup is 'very happy' Blizzard caught the single-target-contingent design and pivoted before live.
ptr.set4: Adds extra Voltaic Blaze stacks plus Crash Lightning CDR. Heavily favors Stormbringer, which has the spare GCDs to weave Voltaic Blaze as a priority; Totemic struggles to juggle it against Storm Unleashed and its totem cadence. Fire Nova becomes a nice single-target pickup but is NOT a mandatory talent swap — a welcome, less-forceful tier-set design. Overall a solid all-rounder giving damage in nearly all situations.
ptr.watch: The 'baggage': both hero trees are all-or-nothing cooldown profiles with little build diversity ('a red Totemic and a blue Stormbringer'); the Doom Winds/Ascendance deck-of-cards RNG is a sore point — a 600-Maelstrom, 3-proc deck that can run ~1000 stacks (~5 min) between procs and doesn't reset without relogging, 'bordering on ruining the feel'; Descending Skies hard-locks Stormbringer to Ascendance with no controlled alternative; and the Crash Lightning damage split stripped Enhancement's traditional priority/funnel strength (Totemic hit hardest — Totemic Rebound fires on the wrong target). It's shaping up like the War Within pattern: Totemic is hit harder by the nerfs and gains less from the buffs/tier set while Stormbringer pulls ahead again. Structure/tuning, not resolved yet.

ptr.theme: The 07-21 rework lands: Unleash Life, Riptide and Farseer all fixed at the root
ptr.summary: Harreks, Wowhead's Restoration Shaman guide writer, reads the 12.1 pass as a big step in the right direction because it targets long-standing design pain points instead of padding numbers until they match. Doubling Unleash Life bakes in the Season 1 2-set so the spell stands on its own rather than being half a spell plus a set bonus, and Earthen Accord's additive +20% makes the follow-up talent do what players always assumed it did. Riptide's doubled periodic healing plus the new Swelling Tides finally make the spec's signature button worth pressing for its own healing. Healing Rain's 6th target is a raid-only ~20% buff that threads the needle Resto has been stuck on all season (good in keys, bad in raid). And the Farseer ancestors' Chain Heal almost triples, making the weaker hero tree genuinely competitive. His direct answer to "is Restoration weak?" is no: where in Season 1 he says you were doing your raid a disservice by bringing it, the spec is now in a very competitive spot and can overshadow other healers when played well.
changes: Farseer Healing Rain reworked — the sole meaningful change.
The other hero tree gets nothing.
Baseline throughput problems remain unaddressed.
PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): Acid Rain damage +50% but now ticks every 2s (was 1s); fixes so Healing Rain heals immediately on cast and both Acid/Healing Rain grant a proper final partial tick.

PTR build (2026-07-21): Resto rework — new talent Swelling Tides (Healing Stream/Stormstream Totem extend active Riptides by 3s); Unleash Life healing +100%; Riptide direct +25% / periodic +100%; Healing Rain now heals up to 6 targets (was 5); Farseer Chain Heal bounces to 5 targets (was 3), loses 10% per jump (was 30%), +50% healing; Calm Waters removed. Venomous Abyss 2-set Healing Rain 8s (was 10s) and 4-set Condensation absorb -30%; Season 1 2-set Unleash Life bonus +50% (was +100%).

PTR build (2026-07-21), detail the review adds: Earthen Accord's Unleash Life bonus is now an ADDITIVE +20% (25%→45%) instead of the old multiplicative 20% (25%→30%); Current Control now also cuts Chain Heal's mana cost by 15% (absorbing the removed Calm Waters); Wavespeaker's Blessing moved up into tier 2 in Calm Waters' old slot; Healing Wave +10%; Farseer ancestors' Chain Heal jump distance 20 yd (was 15).
ptr.set2: Its bonus Healing Rains were cut to 8s specifically to offset Healing Rain's new 6th target — his read is that this keeps the set in check without giving tierset rains a different power level from your own. He also flags the bonus as heavily Totemic-weighted: Totemic's rains heal more, and a hidden Surging Totem passive doubles the Tidewaters / Overflowing Shores / Downpour healing that every extra rain procs.
ptr.set4: The −30% Condensation cut reads to him as a correction, not a nerf: the earlier +300% was an overreaction to a bug where the absorb only ever landed on the shaman who owned the rain. With the bug fixed, the buffed version was a bit too strong, and this lands it in a healthier place. (Pre-06-30 commentary about the absorb being low-impact no longer applies.)
ptr.watch: Mana is still the big question mark — zero active regeneration, and Chain Heal's healing-per-mana is so close to Healing Wave's that Season 1's answer was "cast Chain Heal, then stand still". Healing Wave's +10% and the Current Control merge improve that comparison without solving it; his stated worst case is Resto ending up like Season 1 Holy Paladin, with good numbers gated behind assigned Innervates. Mastery effectiveness sits around 20–30% and remains the most contested stat complaint. Totemic is still expected to be the preferred hero tree, partly because of that unaccounted-for hidden Surging Totem passive. He explicitly declines to predict the healer meta or RWF compositions. A second Earthshrine worry (Seksi, 07-22): the kit keeps accumulating high-impact RNG — the new set hinges on whether Rain procs during damage or downtime and on whom, most Ascendance uptime rides random Riptide procs, and Stormstream Totem banks are luck-dependent going into big damage. His fear is structural: lucky-log showcases plus an M+-leaning kit invite the "opposite Preservation problem" — nerfed for M+ optics before the raid profile ever gets good. His bottom line is still "changes are good, enjoy".

ptr.theme: A grab-bag rework — a couple wins, a couple losses, mostly mediocre
ptr.summary: Archimtiros reads the 12.1 Arms pass as "a couple good changes, a couple bad, and a whole lot of mediocre ones." Rend, Ravager, and Tactical Edge get real reworks, but losing guaranteed Sweeping Strikes uptime raises real questions about Arms as the "2-target pinnacle," and Colossus Smash alignment problems persist. Wowhead's 2026-07-21 12.1 Arms review adds the missing piece behind Arms' PTR standing: it is "performing very well" mostly because of bugs, and the reviewer's own read is "still strong, but uncertain" — expect a tumble of a few spots once they are fixed, while still landing comfortably in the upper tier of Mythic+ damage.
changes: Rend now costs 10 rage and is single-target only; Cleave applies it in AoE. Bloodletting grants 5% ability crit vs Rend targets but no longer extends Rend duration — cheaper, but refresh more often.
Ravager redesigned: +50% damage, no longer buffs Cleave/Whirlwind, and makes enemies take 25%→50% increased bleed damage for 12s; usable in single target again.
Broad Strokes cuts Sweeping Strikes to 6 charges (from 12) and Improved Sweeping Strikes is removed — no more 100% Sweep uptime.
Demolish moved to a flat 30s CD (was variable) but still won't align cleanly with Colossus Smash.
Tactical Edge redesigned so Colossus Smash grants a Sudden Death use; Master Tactician still terrible.

PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): single-target buffs into Slayer — melee auto-attack +100%, the 2-set now boosts both Mortal Strike and Execute (was Mortal Strike only), and Slayer's Dominance proc chance 25% (was 15%); devs targeting Arms/Slayer's lagging single-target.

PTR build (2026-07-21): AoE reshaped to move damage off Cleave — Dreadnaught is now pure AoE (no longer damages the Overpower target) with +100% damage while Cleave -10%; Slayer Opportunist doubled to 20% damage and 20% crit damage on the next Overpower (was 10% each).

Good bugs (Wowhead 12.1 Arms review, 2026-07-21): the S2 2-set's Slam splash (Concussive Slam) unintentionally triggers Mortal Wounds, so every Cleave has a high chance to spread Deep Wounds to ALL nearby targets rather than just the Slam target — worth another +5-9% Deep Wounds damage on top of the splash's own 3-6%, more than doubling the set's multi-target value. Separately, Dreadnaught is now treated as a distinct spell, granting an extra Martial Prowess stack per Overpower and an extra Battlelord reset chance per target — a real gain in the two-target patterns common in Venomous Abyss.

Bad bug (same review, Slayer, present since Midnight launch): Executioner is an "asynchronous" buff — the game tracks one buff plus a removal event per trigger, so procs at the 3-stack cap still schedule a fourth expiry and stacks fall off EARLY (observed ~11s on an 18s buff). The result is less Execute damage and erratic Bladestorm cooldown reduction. Master of Warfare is unaffected (10-stack cap is never exceeded).

Undocumented mitigation for the asynchronous-stacking bug the review leads with: Executioner's maximum stacks raised 3 → 5 (verified in spell data, 07-31). Since the desync only manifests at max stacks, this curtails the worst of it — and doubles as a sizeable Slayer buff to Execute damage and Bladestorm cooldown reduction. The bug itself still exists.

PTR build (2026-07-31): a trim plus a set rework the devs frame as making the current tier set more rewarding than mixing older pieces — Powerful Momentum's Sweeping Strikes chain damage cut to 20% (was 25%) and Execute -15%, against a Venomous Abyss 4-set whose Slam bonus doubles to 20% (was 10%) and now stacks to 5 (was 3), while the Midnight Season 1 2-set's Colossus Smash bonus drops to 3% (was 5%).
ptr.set4: Decent in AoE but terrible in single target, especially measured against S1's universally-powerful set — a real step down on the ST bench. (Pre-07-08 — single-target buffs landed since, incl. Execute joining the 2-set; see Key changes.) The 07-21 review's own verdict on the shipped set: seamless to play and a small step down from S1 on paper, but bug-inflated in Mythic+ right now; the 4-set's 3-stack Slam cap is commonly overflowed during Execute phases. (The 2026-07-31 build answers that last complaint directly — the cap rose to 5 stacks and the per-stack Slam bonus doubled to 20% — while trimming Execute and the S1 2-set to push players onto the current set.)
ptr.watch: Arms' top-of-the-PTR Mythic+ standing rests on bugs (Deep Wounds spreading off the set's Slam splash; Dreadnaught's extra procs) — the open question is how Blizzard rebalances once they are fixed, given most PTR testing is already done. The review still expects Arms comfortably in the upper tier of M+ afterwards. The older worries are unresolved: losing Improved Sweeping Strikes and 100% Sweep uptime puts the "2-target pinnacle" claim in question, and Demolish still won't line up with Colossus Smash.
ptr.sourceLabel: Archimtiros (Icy Veins Arms author, SimC dev, Skyhold)

ptr.theme: A stronger set and genuinely better gameplay — still a master of nothing
ptr.summary: Archimtiros's 2026-07-25 full 12.1 review updates his earlier read: the Raging Blow question he was watching has been answered — Slayer's reworked Hack and Slash now buffs Raging Blow damage instead of refunding charges, giving Slayer a smooth Raging-Blow-focused rotation, and Rampaging Ruin's rework removes its single-target penalty. He calls almost all of the changes objectively good and the Season 2 set a considerable step up in power. His verdict stays mixed because performance hasn't followed: Fury remains a sustained damage dealer in a burst-window meta — "actually quite fun to play, but just kind of mediocre" — with PTR raid performance better than its Mythic+, and average at best in both.
changes: Rend simplified — no longer a standalone button, now applied by Thunder Clap / Whirlwind
Whirlwind now generates 3 Rage innately, opening up single-target use; new Carving Blades gives Whirlwind +50% damage on a single target (choice node vs. Meat Cleaver)
Rampaging Ruin redesigned to be more universal but plays as a talent-point tax — always taken in AoE, forcing you to drop Massacre / Executioner's Wrath / Deep Wounds / Cruelty
Hack and Slash: Rampage has a 75% chance to refund a Raging Blow charge — only matters if Raging Blow is worth using over Bloodthirst, which it currently isn't
Mountain Thane: Thunder Blast +40% but Crashing Thunder cut 30%→10%, making it more RNG-dependent
PTR build 68569 (2026-07-08): Bloodbath rebalanced toward the bleed — initial hit −12%, bleed +300% (dev-stated net-neutral to Bloodbath's overall damage).

2026-07-25 review — Hack and Slash reworked: it now increases Raging Blow's damage and no longer refunds multiple charges, and reduced rage generation outside cooldowns stops the endless Raging Blow/Rampage cycle. Slayer's rotation now has two distinct phases (Recklessness up vs. down) and reads as much healthier.

2026-07-25 review — Rend is gone from the rotation: the new class-tree talent Storm of Blood applies it automatically (functionally identical to live Improved Whirlwind), removing a keybind and the manual-cast decision.

2026-07-25 review — Rampaging Ruin reworked again: Rampage now deals an EXTRA burst of area damage instead of replacing its normal damage, so the old single-target penalty is gone and Mountain Thane can take it freely — but it adds to Fury's multitarget talent tax.

2026-07-25 review — Mountain Thane tuning moved Thunder Clap damage into Thunder Blast, so Bloodthirst-fishing for Thunder Blast procs matters much more and both Fury hero specs are now proc-dependent.

Undocumented alongside it: Frenzy's maximum stacks raised 4 → 10 (verified in spell data, 07-31) — the Fury half of the asynchronous-stacking mitigation; the buff-desync bug only bites at cap, so more headroom means it rarely does.
ptr.set2: 2026-07-25 read: a considerable step up in power from Season 1. The Recklessness caps are reasonably low (Raging Blow only needs three casts), but fitting both Bloodthirst and Raging Blow between Rampage, Execute and Whirlwind/Thunder Clap is a long-standing Fury struggle, and there is no in-game tracker for the stacks. (Pre-07-25 read: capped effects made the set look weak.)
ptr.set4: 2026-07-25 read: Bloodthirst only needs two casts to cap the Recklessness crit bonus, and it matters that it goes up early in the window. Smooth on Slayer (Unhinged auto-casts Bloodthirst); awkward on Mountain Thane, where Thunder Clap and Thunder Blast compete for the same GCDs. (Pre-07-25 read: underwhelming alongside the 2pc.)
ptr.watch: The gameplay questions are answered — what is left is raw performance. Archimtiros puts Fury's PTR raid numbers ahead of its Mythic+ but average at best in both; watch whether a tuning pass before launch lifts a sustained-damage spec in a meta built around burst windows.
ptr.sourceLabel: Archimtiros (Warrior theorycrafter, SimC dev, Skyhold) — Wowhead 12.1 Fury review, 2026-07-25

ptr.summary: Mwahi/Archimtiros read it as a grab bag: some changes are good and make sense, others are really questionable, but gameplay-wise nothing actually changes. The defensive and Execute-support tweaks are welcome, while the Ravager bleed direction feels off-brand — "seems like we're being turned into a budget Assassination Rogue."

Ravager +50% damage, but the bleed focus is weird — 'budget Assassination Rogue' territory

ptr.set4: Insignificant on the bleed side, with some AoE potential at best. (Pre-07-08 — the bleed was since doubled.)
ptr.watch: The Ravager/tier-set bleed pivot is the thing to watch — Archimtiros is skeptical it fits Prot's identity, and with the 2pc leaning on RNG procs the set may not move the needle even as Execute and defensives get healthier.
